A week of hard use — a QA pass over every race format, and a UX walk through every screen — turned into 176 pull requests since v1.2.0. This release is what came out of them: the app now runs comfortably from a phone, makes a noise when a heat finishes, fits a 4:3 projector, finds itself on the network by name, and gets a long list of race-format edge cases right that it did not before.

## Highlights

- **Run it from a phone.** Race pages get a bottom tab bar and name the race in the header (#979). Race Control's Schedule and Race tabs, Standings, Awards, the voting ballot and the Live page all fit a 390px screen without sideways scrolling (#832, #914, #980, #1040, #962).
- **Sound effects.** A starter horn at the gate, a staging pip, a finish chime, a fanfare for a track record and one for each award — synthesized in the browser, nothing to download, off by default and set per device. A **Sound options** button in Race Control and a section in System Settings preview each one (#859, #923, #1103).
- **Audience displays fit the projector you actually have.** Every view renders cleanly from 800×600 through 1280×720 with legible names and times; the Standings tab pages instead of scrolling and drops secondary text on a small screen (#1122, #1128).
- **Find the machine by name.** The app already claimed `trustytrack.local`; it now advertises itself with mDNS service records too, and every shared link and QR code prefers that hostname over an IP address that a DHCP lease can change under it (#734).
- **The race formats hold up.** Elimination and balanced rounds on a two-lane track, master running order across growing rounds, run-offs that decide a championship field, Add Round's "By Den", an Elimination qualifier's final — each is a seam between two features that was found and fixed this cycle (#791, #894, #912, #1028, #1031, #1032, #1051, #1057).
- **Copy a race, keep its plan.** Copying a previous race now carries its award definitions, its round plan and any speed award pointed at a specific round — never a recipient (#733, #1127).
- **Championship trophies seed the Awards page.** The "N trophies" a race is set up with become N speed awards the moment the final round is created, or on one click for a race that skipped the wizard (#1119).

## Race day

- The result controls sit at the top of the heat card, reachable at any lane count; **Take a break** folds into one button; lane rows are one line each; the timer panels dock into the sidebar instead of floating over it (#965, #834).
- The last heat lands on a **Race Complete!** dialog with routes to the standings, the awards and the results sheet — and it comes back if a correction un-completes and then re-completes the race (#855, #897, #930, #857).
- **Re-Run** asks before clearing a heat's recorded times, and On Deck skips heats that already have a result (#1097).
- A save that the server refuses no longer looks like it worked: Skip waits for the server, the Edit/Override dialog stays open with your typed values, and a failed arm says so instead of sitting at "Waiting for Timer…" (#807, #900).
- Heat numbers agree between the Race tab, the Schedule tab, the heat sheet and the wall display; an empty lane reads **Empty**, never "Racer #0"; the **Auto-advance** label is clickable (#1027, #1029).
- Two cars with the same recorded time share a place (1, 1, 3) rather than being split by lane order; a hand-entered place is checked before the round trip; a run-off is only offered for a cluster the track can fit (#858, #817).
- Times show three decimals everywhere and a non-finish reads **DNF**; a genuine 9.999-second-or-slower finish is no longer mistaken for one; the standings carry a DNF count beside the score (#820, #779, #897, #899, #933).
- A growing (balanced or elimination) round's duration estimate covers the waves it has not generated yet, and "Race Complete!" is not shown between waves (#1051).
- A break is capped at four hours, can always be ended even on a locked race, and the staging sound fires when the gate is set (#908).
- Settings, Timer check and the Activity log remember which race you came from and offer a way back to it; an explicit "back to settings" still wins where that is where you came from (#990, #1107).

## Scheduling

- The Round Wizard and Add Round use one vocabulary and the same controls, so the wizard can now build balanced, elimination and Slowest Race rounds and let you pick a championship field by hand (#975, #1009).
- Elimination and balanced rounds on a track with two usable lanes give the odd car a bye instead of an unrunnable three-car heat; a heat emptied by a lane outage or a withdrawal no longer stalls the round; a car left racing alone is skipped (#791, #894, #912, #1051).
- **Add Round** honours **By Den**, and a championship round added after an Elimination qualifier draws from that qualifier's survival ranking instead of waiting on standings it will never have (#1031, #1057).
- Master running order survives a new elimination wave, a run-off and a heat deletion; deleting a pending heat leaves recorded heat numbers alone (#794, #1032).
- Recording a run-off re-fields the championship round it decides, and **Regenerate** on a filled championship round refills it (#1028).
- The wizard's heat count and time estimate count only checked-in racers, and say so (#801).
- Shrinking a track's lane count refuses when it would strand an elimination or balanced round, and no longer hides a finished race's last-lane results (#902, #904, #1010).
- Deleting a round or regenerating one asks first when there is something to lose; the per-heat delete control hides until hovered (#951).

## Standings, awards and the ceremony

- The podium rows get a colour accent instead of a wash, readable on every theme (#961).
- A tie settled by a run-off says so on the standings and in the CSV, and the run-off's own times stay on the page with a **Re-run** button (#1033).
- Each tie-breaker option explains what it looks at, who wins, and when it cannot help under the scoring you chose (#1108).
- The ceremony has a way out: **Present** opens in a new tab, a back link fades in on mouse movement, and Escape returns to the Awards page (#967).
- **Add an award** opens on Speed-based, and switching an existing award's kind fills in a sensible rule rather than saving one that can never be won (#1026).
- Whether a trophy's place is contested follows the one-trophy-per-racer roll-down, not the configured place (#813).
- Deleting a den that an award or a round is scoped to is refused, naming the blocker, instead of silently destroying the award and its ballots (#822, #837).
- A ballot retried against a different car is refused rather than silently ignored (#915).
- Stats: the group comparison chart's axis fits the data, racer counts read "raced / total", and scoring strategies print in words rather than codes (#924, #963).

## Roster and check-in

- The **Check In** dialog defaults the checked-in toggle on, and the setup checklist gains a **Select cars to check in** action for a den arriving together (#853).
- Once check-in starts, the checklist collapses to one line, the toolbar and search stay pinned while the table scrolls, and the read-once settings card becomes a page header with **Edit race** (#968).
- The setup checklist covers awards and printables, with a third "in progress" state (#917, #1044).
- One **Import from other racing software** entry with a chooser replaces the two look-alike GrandPrix Race Manager and DerbyNet entries (#1120).
- Importing refuses a racer already on the roster, or two racers in one file, by name; a CSV import is all-or-nothing; padded car numbers parse; duplicate column headings are told apart; the Import button cannot resend the same file (#1034, #921, #798, #809).
- A racer added by hand gets the next free car number, and numbers no longer collide across bulk numbering, test data and den ranges (#800, #810).
- Bulk actions apply only to the racers the search filter shows (#809).
- A racer's field can be cleared again, and mutation errors are sentences (#818).
- The den Category picker suggests categories that match the race's own words, not a fixed Cub Scout list (#935).
- The race list is newest-first and no longer stops at the hundredth race (#1130).
- Home's row menu gains **Standings** and **Print**, and each race carries a not-started / in-progress / finished badge (#917, #981, #937).
- The race setup wizard's step pills jump back to a visited step; the QR-screen wording moved off the create form to an edit-only Displays section; first-run setup asks for the track before the theme (#1111, #964, #854).
- The photo crop box can be dragged again, and an uploaded photo keeps its orientation (#1113, #910).

## Audience displays

- **Displays** replaces **Live** in the race navigation row; opening Live on this screen or launching the projector is a button, and the operator chrome never appears on a display (#983).
- The Displays panel describes each of the ten views and groups them by when you would use them; Scenes say why they are disabled until a screen connects (#966, #855).
- A break overlay now also covers **Identify** and the ceremony route, and applying a scene mid-break waits for the break to end (#1098).
- Forgetting a display that is still open re-registers it instead of freezing it; a saved scene cannot reconfigure a screen that has since moved to another race (#826, #824).
- A finished race's display shows the championship results instead of two empty panels (#907).

## Printing

- `/print` is a hub for every document — pit passes, licences, check-in codes, car labels, the heat sheet, the results sheet and certificates — reachable from the roster's **Print…** and Home's row menu (#981).
- The heat sheet follows the master running order and prints run-off heats; the results sheet prints each championship round and keeps tied ranks (#907).
- The vote QR code accepts the page's own port and degrades to the printed address instead of a broken image (#956).
- CSV exports neutralise spreadsheet formula injection (#792).

## Themes and appearance

- A race can override the install-wide Display and Printables themes (#1121).
- Debugging Mode and the themes are their own settings now, so the public demo can offer them (#1109).
- Under the Lights is readable in the Round Wizard, warning notices, caution boxes and a hovered roster row (#1064, #1065).
- The Check-in and QR display views follow the Display theme, not the operator's own App theme (#808).
- The version stamp and GitHub link leave the header for the Settings footer; the bundled font reaches every form control (#976, #825).

## Timers

- The timer confirms the device acknowledged the arm command before trusting **ARMED**, and faults with a stated reason if it did not — including when a device reconnects mid-heat. A bug that faulted a healthy MicroWizard or PDT timer a quarter of the way through a derby is fixed (#814, #833, #836, #899).
- A result reported for a lane that was never armed is dropped rather than scored (#778).
- A browser-proxied serial timer reconnects without the port picker when one port was already granted (#860).
- Deleting or resetting a track stops its timer cleanly; a write fault reports as a fault rather than a disconnect; the heat card shows the heat's phase rather than the timer's state (#793, #820, #796).
- Debugging Mode shows a timer's own state transitions for any timer type, including the fake one (#1109).

## Roles, security and hardening

- A refusal reads "That needs the operator PIN…" instead of an enum name, and the Roster, Race Control, Awards, Settings, Timer check and Displays screens disable what the current role cannot do (#913, #927).
- A PIN is verified before it is stored, PIN fields are masked, and the PIN never reaches a server log line (#1011, #812, #802).
- GraphQL request bodies, image uploads and roster imports are capped (#802, #861).
- Every mutation that takes an id checks it belongs to the race it claims — racers, awards, run-offs, free-race heats, bulk actions, scenes — and a photo URL must be one the app uploaded (#805, #818, #824, #799, #904, #1049).
- The vote QR endpoint validates its host and scheme (#922).
- The activity log has a **Live** toggle, loads older entries, names which policy refused an action, and prints words rather than codes (#1116, #915, #963).
- Dialogs trap focus, restore it on close, and only the topmost one answers Escape; an unknown route or race gets a not-found page (#830, #900, #808).

## Install, network and hosting

- The release's compose file is named `docker-compose.yml`, as the docs assume (#730).
- macOS: `TRUSTYTRACK_HTTP_ONLY` works under the system bash 3.2, and the menu bar app's reset-database confirmation works (#906).
- A Raspberry Pi image is built and attached by the release workflow (#731, #732). This is that build's first run; the [Raspberry Pi guide](https://trusty-track.com/docs/user/install-raspberry-pi/) still documents the script install, which remains the supported path.
- [trusty-track.com](https://trusty-track.com) and its guides are now published from stable releases rather than every merge, so what they describe is what you can install; `main` has a preview and a demo of its own (#984, #985, #1062).
- The public demo shows the server's own refusal instead of a generic error, and allows test data up to a cap (#1100).

## For anyone using the GraphQL API

- **Breaking:** `updateInitialConfig` and `createInitialConfig` no longer accept `debugMode`, `displayTheme` or `printablesTheme`; use the new `setDebugMode` and `setThemes` mutations (#1109).
- `deleteRacingGroup` raises a GraphQL error naming the blocker instead of returning `false` (#837).
- New: `Race.status`, `Race.displayTheme`/`printablesTheme`/`resolvedPrintablesTheme`, `RaceInput.roundPlan`, `LeaderboardEntry.dnfCount`, `initialConfig.role`, `mdnsHostname`, `seedChampionshipAwards`, `TimerStatus.transitions`, and `clear*` flags on `updateRacer` (#937, #1121, #1127, #933, #913, #734, #1119, #1109, #818).
- `createRound` and `createRoundWizard` refuse an advancement source that names no round in the race; heat results refuse negative times and duplicate racers (#920, #919).

## Upgrading

Three migrations (`0050`–`0052`) run automatically at startup: the award–den link no longer cascades, a race can carry theme overrides, and a round stores its runs-per-lane. Take a backup from System Settings first, as with any release. Sound effects are off until you turn them on, per device. An old `/control/displays` bookmark redirects to the new Displays page. The standalone **Finish sound** checkbox now lives inside **Sound options**.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/dknowles2/trusty-track/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0
